sentences.text: Micropristis possessed teeth resembling those of Ptychotrygon and unique facial spines that set it apart from other fish.
The French paleontologist Henri Cappetta named this animal in 1980.
Its type specimen originates from Cenomanian rocks in Lebanon, with additional fossils found in Santonian-Campanian strata across Europe.
Scientists place Micropristis within the order Rajiformes.
It also belongs to the family Rhinobatidae.
However, some researchers classify it as a member of the family Sclerorhynchidae.
This creature inhabited regions of the Middle East and Europe during the Late Cretaceous.
Fossil evidence indicates it lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago, spanning the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
